headline: Large Energy User Grid Cost Shifting
short_summary: This bill shifts the financial burden of grid infrastructure upgrades for large energy users, such as data centers, from residential ratepayers to the corporations themselves.
status: Last Action: Approved by Governor-Chapter 1123 (effective 7/1/2026) on 2026-05-14
opponents: Data center industry, large energy users.
news_headline: Governor Signs Bills Shifting Data Center Energy Costs.
news_summary: Governor Spanberger signed legislation directing regulators to assign electricity costs to data centers, preventing these expenses from being passed to residential customers. This aims to address rising energy costs partly due to data center expansion.

headline: Data Center Water Consumption Reporting
short_summary: This bill mandates data centers to publicly report their water usage, increasing transparency regarding their environmental footprint.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, local communities, water conservation advocates.
news_headline: Potomac Conservancy Pushes for Data Center Water Transparency.
news_summary: Potomac Conservancy advocates for SB 553, a bill requiring data centers to report water usage to the State Water Control Board. This transparency is crucial for protecting the Potomac River region's water supply amidst rapid data center expansion.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise Limits
short_summary: This bill establishes regulations for the siting of data centers and sets limits on operational noise, addressing community quality of life concerns.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local communities, residents near proposed data center sites, environmental groups.
news_headline: Loudoun County Grapples with Growing Data Center Noise.
news_summary: Residents in Loudoun County are experiencing constant noise from data centers, impacting their quality of life. Local officials are discussing mitigation efforts and potential changes to noise ordinances to address these concerns.
